correctness.rationale: On nonconstant eigenmodes, μ/(d−μ)=μ/d+μ²/[d(d−μ)]. For connected d-regular G the first sum is −1 after division by d; the second is at least (Nd−d²)/(2d²) since μ≥−d. This gives tr(AL⁺)≥(N−3d)/(2d). Equality at N=3d would require every nonconstant μ to be 0 or −d. The trace then forces a single −d, but the second moment requires a nonconstant squared sum of 2d², not d². Thus an actual edge has L⁺_uv>0 by the undirected edge trace sum. Completing the square in the scalar numerator gives positivity, the denominator is no smaller for h≥0, and the constant mode is fixed. Expansion on each positive Laplacian eigenmode gives T=I−12L⁺/h+O(h^(−2)), establishing negativity on the fixed edge for all sufficiently large finite h without instability. For C_3 square C_3 use the constant and orthogonal complement projectors of each K_3 factor: with A=3h²+3h+1 and B=3h²+6h+4 one gets R(3h)=1−12h/B and R(6h)=1−6h/A. The adjacent and nonadjacent coefficients give 4h(h+1)/(AB) and 2h²(3h+2)/(AB); subtracting four of each from 1 yields the claimed diagonal. The entries are strictly positive at h>0 and at h=0 the matrix is I. All other tori in the stated range have N≥12 and d=4, so fail unconditional positivity. The exact-rational support and recorded output were inspected but not executed; the all-graph result does not depend on the seven finite regressions.

evidence: The authors' 2011 slides (p. 22) give n<3k as necessary for the M-property in distance-regular graphs of diameter ≥2. The edge trace is d tr(L⁺)−(N−1), equivalently a Kirchhoff-index test Kf(G)>N(N−1)/d for strict positivity of that sum.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The M-property concerns the signs of all off-diagonal entries of L⁺. Its failure is necessary for, but not equivalent to, showing a positive entry on an edge. Resistance of an edge detects its sign only after comparison to the sum of the two pseudoinverse diagonal entries. The edge trace formulation does not require a constant diagonal or distance regularity.

value.rationale: Distinguishing preservation of nonnegative data from spectral stability matters for graph heat integration. The sufficient condition depends only on coarse graph structure and locates a failing transition on an existing edge without a graph-specific calculation. It also settles all cycle-product sizes in the stated range, rather than extrapolating from a few grids or claiming that all positive steps fail.
